questions.question: What three parts of an HTTP response does ResponseEntity represent?
questions.explanation: ResponseEntity wraps the whole reply: the status code, the headers and the body.

questions.question: Which return type says that the response has no body, such as after a delete?
questions.explanation: Void means there is never a body. Combine it with noContent().build() to send 204.

questions.question: A method returns ResponseEntity.created(URI.create("/bookings/5")).body(booking). Which status and header does the client see?
questions.explanation: created(uri) sets status 201 and puts the address of the new item in the Location header.

questions.question: A controller returns ResponseEntity.notFound().build() for GET /bookings/9. What does the client receive?
questions.explanation: notFound() sets 404, and build() finishes the entity without a body.

questions.question: A developer returns ResponseEntity.ok(null) when a booking is missing. What is the problem?
options: The client gets 200, so it thinks the call succeeded, and should get 404 with notFound().build()
Spring throws a NullPointerException at startup
questions.explanation: A 200 with an empty body hides the missing item. A 404 tells the client the booking does not exist.
